failures.clause: **Flaky tests.** A flaky test is one that passes and fails on the *same code* (Luo et al. 2014; Parry et al. 2021 — both cited in the literature). Detection requires observing both verdicts at the same commit. NYX already groups runs by (system, artifact, kind, title) in C-009 and C-007, so the same grouping identifies flakiness: same defined test, same declared commit *and* environment, one pass and one fail.

failures.clause: **C. A cross-critic meta-critic.** A critic that receives the *other critics' results* as its context and reports only *interactions*: two critics disagreeing, two critics firing on one defect, a critic whose `no_finding` is contradicted by another's FINDING. This is the "niche criticism" the question asks about — it is the only shape that catches a class of defect no single rule can see. It needs a context extension (`CriticContext` currently has no field for peer results) and it must be deterministic, so it is a Phase 2-class change, not a tweak.
